The strongest anomaly is **M5**. Its Vds is 25 mV against a Vdsat of 177 mV, so it sits deep in triode. Its W/L of 11.63/1 is 5.8× the bias device M6 (W/L 2/1), so the intended mirror ratio isn't being delivered. Tail current is 12.9 µA where the mirror would give about 58 µA, and the error-amp gm/Id and loop behavior are set by that tail. M1 and Mp rank next because they have the largest ripple sensitivities, and Cc is third because a 35 fF compensation cap is small enough to be a corrupted value, though its absence from the sensitivity list makes it less likely.

It is pushed into triode (Vds=0.025 V < Vdsat=0.177 V), so the tail current is set by the diff-pair/node voltage instead of the mirror, which degrades error-amp gm and loop behavior and leaves the output ringing (0.70 V p-p settled ripple)."}
